findings.claim: Unrelated change to the serializer runtime: the `case <= byte.MaxValue` branch (UInt8 encoding) is removed from the integer writer in MessagePackPrimitives.Writers.cs. Values 128..255 will now be written as UInt16 (0xcd) instead of UInt8 (0xcc). That changes the wire bytes and bloats the output. It is out of scope for REQ-2283 (a generator/analyzer crash), and it breaks the compact-encoding behavior. Numeric serialization is flagged as bug-prone in [L13].

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize the values 128 and 255 as uint/int with base-built and head-built MessagePack and compare bytes. Base emits 0xcc 0x80 and 0xcc 0xff; head emits 0xcd 0x00 0x80 and 0xcd 0x00 0xff. Also run the MessagePackWriter/MessagePackPrimitives tests.

findings.claim: The new `ReportIfLocatedInCompilation` filter drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a tree of the current compilation. Diagnostics created with a null or None location are silently swallowed, for example MemberNeedsKey on an inherited member of a base type from a referenced assembly. [L17] shows this case has no recorded preference. The filter is also broader than the fix the requirement asks for: guarding the `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` calls. Requirement scope is 'do not crash'. The diagnostics for the metadata members are suppressed on purpose, which fits [L12], but that fit is not an explicit decision for diagnostics on members inherited into compilation-owned types.

receipt_plan.detail: Write an analyzer test where a source [MessagePackObject] class derives from a base class in a referenced assembly that has a public member without [Key]. Compare base and head for MsgPack004. The test fails at head if the diagnostic that was previously reported is now dropped.

findings.claim: The new docs state that diagnostics for members of referenced-assembly types are 'reported by the defining project'. This matches the deliberate exit in [L12] that metadata types get no diagnostic or formatter in the consuming assembly. [L12] says the lack of a diagnostic is not a defect. The generic-closed branch bypasses that early return, which is why the crash appeared, so the new filter aligns it with [L12].

receipt_plan.detail: [L12] Types from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed; a missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect.

questions.text: Should the consuming assembly's generated resolver include a formatter for the closed generic struct from the referenced assembly (Item<int>)? Should it rely on the defining assembly's resolver instead?
options: Include a formatter for Item<int> in the consuming resolver
Rely on the defining assembly's resolver and registration
questions.why_it_matters: If the answer is 'include', the tests need to assert a formatter in the generated output. The tests currently use SkipGeneratedSourcesCheck and check only the resolver hint name. If the answer is 'rely on the defining assembly', the current change is sufficient. [L16] records no preference, only 'follow the requirement', and the requirement asks only for a generated resolver.
